name: Intuitive Surgical, Inc.
fiscal_year_note: FY = calendar year (Jan-Dec). Latest reported quarter is Q3 2026, released Oct 20, 2026. Next report (Q4/FY2026 and 2027 guidance) expected Jan 21, 2027 (Yahoo earnings date).

latest_quarter.label: Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep 2026)
latest_quarter.operating_margin_basis: non-GAAP (applies to gross margin, operating margin and EPS). GAAP gross margin 68.4%; GAAP operating margin 19.4% ($592.6M) after a $450M antitrust settlement charge ($454.9M booked in SG&A); GAAP diluted EPS $1.49 (non-GAAP $3.00, vs $2.40 a year earlier).

guidance: FY2026 (updated Oct 20, 2026): worldwide da Vinci procedure growth 14%-15%, expected near the midpoint (narrowed from 13.5%-15.5% in April and 13%-15% in January); non-GAAP gross margin 68.7%-69.3%, including ~0.9% of revenue net tariff impact after refunds (January guide was 67%-68% with a 1.2% tariff hit; April was 67.5%-68.5% with 1.0%); non-GAAP opex growth 11%-13%; stock-based comp $860-870M; other income $300-310M; Q4 non-GAAP tax rate 22% +/-0.5 pt. Pricing changes ahead: (1) China charge-code policy changes will cut I&A prices in China 'significantly' starting November 2026; (2) an expanded extended-use instrument program starting 1H 2027 (U.S. first, pending 510(k) clearance; Europe 2H 2027) will lower da Vinci I&A revenue per procedure by ~3%-5% on a constant-mix basis once fully implemented, building through 2027. Long-term non-GAAP operating margin framework 35%-40% (1H 2026 ran at 41%), so excess margin may be reinvested. 2027 guidance will come in January 2027. Consensus Q4 2026 (Yahoo): revenue $3.23B, EPS $2.95.

physical_ai_exposure.description: All revenue comes from robot-assisted surgery and robotic bronchoscopy: da Vinci multiport (Xi and da Vinci 5), da Vinci SP, and Ion. Installed base at Sep 30, 2026: 12,094 da Vinci systems (+12%, including 2,000+ da Vinci 5) and 1,152 Ion (+21%); customers averaged 10,000+ procedures per day in Q3. Q3 2026: 546 da Vinci placements (+28%; U.S. 335, OUS 211), including 315 da Vinci 5 and a record 42 SP; 56 Ion placements; 291 placements under operating leases (160 usage-based). da Vinci 5 handled more than a quarter of U.S. procedures in Q3 (13% a year earlier) and runs above installed-base utilization. Average purchased system price is ~$1.6M. Recurring revenue (instruments, services, leases) was 86% of revenue in Q1 2026. Q3 procedure growth: da Vinci +14% (U.S. +10%, OUS +20%; Europe +20%, Asia +19%, rest of world +22%), Ion +31%.
physical_ai_exposure.optionality_notes: Robotics is the whole business, so there is no separate 'robotics optionality' to carve out. Upside optionality: AI features (voice-activated UI, automated fourth-arm control); CEO Dave Rosa said 'AI controlled motion and surgery has the potential to improve efficiency and outcomes' but that adoption is early and must earn the confidence of regulators and surgeons; several telesurgery clearances are expected in 1H 2028; da Vinci 5 is cleared for cardiac procedures in the U.S., Europe, India, Japan and Korea; Intuitive plans to accelerate expansion into countries it does not serve today in 2027. No analyst sum-of-the-parts was found in the sources reviewed. The market pays ~37.5x forward earnings (40x 2026 and 36x 2027 consensus EPS), a premium to typical medtech, for the durability of the procedure-driven razor/razor-blade model.

cost_and_supply_chain_notes: Tariff-related risk factors name Mexico (where most instruments and accessories are made), Germany (endoscopes) and China (certain imported materials). The 2026 gross margin guide includes ~0.9% of revenue net tariff impact (down from 1.2% guided in January); Q3 2026 included a $28M one-time refund of IEEPA tariffs ($22M after tax, $0.06/share). Guidance assumes tariffs in effect persist through year-end; the company warns additional tariffs could be material. In April 2026 higher freight and semiconductor memory costs partly offset lower tariffs. In China, products are made and sold through the Intuitive Surgical-Fosun Medical Technology (Shanghai) joint venture (majority-owned; $131.6M noncontrolling interest). On Mar 1, 2026 Intuitive acquired its da Vinci and Ion distributors in Italy, Spain, Portugal, Malta and San Marino for ~$533M net, moving to direct sales there.
debt_notes: No borrowings: no debt on the balance sheet and no interest expense line (leases not counted here). Interest and other income, net, was $75.8M in Q3 2026 ($243.6M for 9M); 2026 other income guided at $300-310M. Cash, cash equivalents and investments fell to $6.80B at Sep 30, 2026 (from $9.03B at Dec 31, 2025) after heavy buybacks: 7.8M shares for $2.94B in Q3 2026 (average ~$377/share).
customer_concentration: No customer at 10% or more of revenue was disclosed in the sources reviewed; customers are hospitals and health systems worldwide. Geographic concentration: the U.S. was 67.7% of Q3 2026 revenue ($2.063B, +20% YoY); OUS $0.986B (+25%). U.S. bariatrics is now 'a little bit over 2%' of global da Vinci procedures. The pending $450M class settlement covers U.S. customers' claims about third-party instrument remanufacturing and servicing.
key_drivers: Procedure growth: da Vinci +14% in Q3 2026 and 14%-15% guided for 2026, with OUS (+20%) outpacing the U.S. (+10%)
da Vinci 5 upgrade cycle: 315 of 546 Q3 placements; 870 placed in 2025; 2,000+ installed; >25% of U.S. procedures; OUS da Vinci 5 placements rose from 12 to 41 YoY
Capital strength: Q3 systems revenue +30% to $769M; U.S. net placements +41%; record SP placements (42)
Ion lung biopsy: procedures +31%, installed base +21%
Margins: non-GAAP gross margin 69.9% and operating margin 41.6% in Q3 2026; tariff headwind easing (1.2% of revenue guided in Jan to ~0.9%)
Japan reimbursement changes in June 2026 are accelerating procedure growth; direct distribution in Italy/Spain/Portugal since March 2026
Capital return: $2.94B buyback in Q3 2026 near the July lows
key_risks: Pricing: China I&A price cut from November 2026 plus 2027 extended-use instruments (~3%-5% lower I&A revenue per procedure) will weigh on 2027 revenue growth
U.S. deceleration: U.S. da Vinci procedure growth slowed to 10% in Q3 2026 (15% in 2025); the U.S. is ~60% of procedures
GLP-1 drugs: U.S. da Vinci bariatric procedures fell ~10% in Q1 2026, attributed to GLP-1 use; management calls it a 'stable decline' that 'hasn't yet approached zero'
China: low tender volumes, intense local robotic competition and lower win rates; only 4 placements in Q1 2026 (17 in Q4 2025); ~250 systems left in the current quota
Competition: Medtronic Hugo (U.S. urology launch), modular systems in ambulatory surgery centers, and Chinese local players
Tariffs on Mexico-made instruments and German endoscopes; legal: the $450M antitrust settlement still needs court approval (decision expected 2027)
Hospital capital budgets and U.S. policy (management says it is too early to judge 340B effects on capital); 2026 YTD stock is down ~20%
